transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
The U.S. government is restricting Chinese companies from accessing American AI technology
through overseas data centers, as NPR's Katie McHugh reports.
While there have been export restrictions on physical trips to China for several years,
a loophole existed that allowed Chinese companies to gain remote access to American AI technology.
The new rule replaces a Biden-era framework to regulate global access to advanced AI chips,
which the Trump administration never enforced.
The move comes amid the fallout from NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected
Chinese spy.
Huang had lobbied President Trump to relax chip export restrictions to China.
Huang resigned from NVIDIA last week, Katie McHugh, NPR News, New York.
President Trump is on his way to Asia, he's due in the Philippines in a couple of hours
before traveling on to China Wednesday, where he is to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping
and Russian leader Vladimir Putin.
Trump said Monday he may also meet with North Korea's Kim Jong-un.
United Airlines' attack outage at delayed departures Monday has been resolved and that
there are no indications of a cybersecurity issue.
And officials believe United's outage is not connected to Friday's air traffic control
outage that led to the FAA grounding planes nationwide on Friday.
NPR's Joel Rose says that outage is under investigation.
The exact details are still under investigation, but there were some warnings about exactly
this scenario.
In a report that was released just in September by the General Accountability Office, the
GAO report noted that the administration has been speeding up the timeline of modernization
work that was already underway, including on this exact telecommunications network that
apparently failed on Friday.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says it remains unclear why a router installed by
an FAA contractor in a facility in Arkansas triggered Friday's ground stop.
At least six people were injured after Ukraine launched a large-scale drone attack on targets
in Russia and the occupied territories.
NPR's Charles Mains reports from Moscow and Ukraine's response to Russia's ongoing attacks
on Ukraine's civilian energy infrastructure ahead of the winter months.
What appeared to mark the largest combined drone counterattack by Kiev since Russia launched
its full-scale invasion nearly five years ago, Russia said its air defenses successfully
intercepted the Ukrainian barrage, a claim that stood at odds with reports of damage
at several large Russian oil and industrial facilities, also hit the lone bridge linking
occupied Crimea to mainland Russia, a project seen as a physical symbol of Russia's hold
over the peninsula, it illegally annexed from Ukraine back in 2014.
The local Moscow-backed authorities reported a halt to traffic along the bridge.
The Kremlin later dismissed the damage as minor.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
And you're listening to NPR News.
And Sudan archaeologists have discovered the original floor of a medieval cathedral dating
back more than a thousand years.
Historians say the church is one of the most important Christian buildings in Africa's
history, as St. Pierre's Jewel Bright reports.
Researchers say the Great Church of Jesus was the largest and most important church
in Medivhia Makuria, one of the early Christian kingdoms that emerged along the Nile River
in Northern Africa following the arrival of Christian missionaries in the 6th century.
The site of the church was first discovered by a team of Polish and Sudanese archaeologists
in 2021, but the cathedral's massive walls made excavation challenging.
The excavating team says they removed substantial layers of accumulated debris before they reached
the cathedral's original levels.
Researchers say the cathedral could have influenced the development of religious architecture
across Africa in the same way Istanbul's Hagia Sophia influenced religious architecture
across Europe and the rest of the world.
And you're listening to NPR News Zegas.
J.P. Morgan Chase, blaming a software bug that caused problems throughout the financial
system Monday.
Chase calls the problems an isolated incident and not the result of a cyber attack.
The tech issue resulted in thousands of customers reporting difficulty accessing online accounts,
as well as problems that several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service sell.
Asian shares declining after AI stocks tumbled on Wall Street, South Korea's tech-heavy benchmark
and shares in Taiwan are both down more than 2 percent.
I'm Jyle Snyder, NPR News.

topics.text: US restricts Chinese companies' remote access to American AI technology via overseas data centers
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid fallout from affair with suspected Chinese spy
Trump travels to Philippines, then China to meet Xi Jinping and Putin; may meet Kim Jong-un
United Airlines resolves delayed-departure outage, says no cybersecurity issue indicated
FAA router failure in Arkansas under investigation after nationwide ground stop Friday
Ukraine drone attack hits Russian targets, including lone bridge linking Crimea to Russia
Sudan archaeologists uncover original floor of 1,000-year-old medieval Makuria cathedral
JPMorgan Chase blames software bug for Monday banking disruptions, rejects cyber attack
Asian tech shares fall after AI stocks tumble on Wall Street
